chapter: Guitar, John Collins and Ellington on the radio
title: Meeting John Collins at 15 and the later quartet in Los Angeles
summary: Jones met Collins professionally when the trio performed, and years later joined Collins's quartet in Los Angeles; Collins stayed with Nat Cole for his family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: When did you first meet John Collins in Chicago?
Is this John or John Levy?
No, we're back to John Collins. We were talking about John Levy off the tape. We'll get to John Levy on the tape in a minute.
Okay.
Unless you want to . Do you want to talk about John Levy now?
No, it doesn't make any difference --
Because you mentioned that your singing trio worked --
Oh, yeah.
And I just wondered, you know, when you and John met and got to know each other.
I was about 15 years old, you know, and --
Was he in the same school you were?
No, I just met him professionally.
Uh-huh.

The trio came in and did a thing at this club. We were chaperoned and everything, you know. And John Collins was playing, and by all three of us playing the little guitar, he attracted us, the way he sounded on his instrument, you know? And he's been an influence musically ever since. Because -- all the guys were kidding me -- well, I'm getting back too late now. When we had the quartet going.
Oh, the one that you had here in Los Angeles.
Yeah, with John. And it was great therapy for me at that time. I think one night when Harry Edison came into the club, said, 'How did you get this guy to the house?'
(Laughter)
So John, he was asking me, 'Would you like to make it with me with this [quartet]?' Before he finished the question I said yes.
(Laughter)
That was it, you know? See, and I don't
know any other people that would work with -- oh, that fast, jump at the opportunity that quick, you know? And that goes all the way back.
To when you were teenagers.

Yeah. It goes all the way back. I said -- because I don't think John had a chance to really stretch out, as we call it, because he was working with Nat Cole, King Cole, you know, and he had a thing about his family. He wanted to raise his daughters. So consequently he wanted something pretty stable, you know?
Yeah, I know.
And which I can understand perfectly. I think we missed a lot musically, but he had to make his own mind up about that, you know?
Yes.
And now that they're grown, his kids, he's coming out more, you know.
If he can get loose from his grandson.
Oh, no, I don't think -- oh, Alfie?
(Laughter)
Oh, those guys are -- they're real buddies.
Yeah.
I don't think -- he can't get away from that. And I wouldn't either, because he's a fine kid, you know? So --
